Home / The system

The system

The last step. Made a standard.

CDIS is an installed, written, trained way of finishing the official paper records your organisation produces. In about ninety seconds, printed pages become a permanently sealed, tamper evident hard cover record.

One lifecycle, three disciplines

Package · Present · Preserve

Built on Peleman Industries document technology, engineered in Belgium since 1939 and operating in more than 120 countries, and operationalised for Nigerian organisations as CDIS.

ILifecycle phase

Package

Printed pages become a permanently sealed, tamper evident document set. A steel spine and thermal seal close the bundle for good. No punching, no tearing, no reopening without visible destruction.

  • Steel spine · thermal seal
  • About ninety seconds per cycle
  • Up to eight documents at once on Elite
  • No punching · no tearing

IILifecycle phase

Present

Book quality, lay flat, hard cover output carrying the organisation's name. Identical across every office, every team member, every matter. The document argues before anyone speaks.

  • Hard cover · lay flat opening
  • Your name on every record
  • Identical output, every office
  • A cover chosen for its purpose

IIILifecycle phase

Preserve

Every record archived in the exact sealed state in which it was presented, and retrievable quickly. Physical documents carry direct evidentiary value across their full retention period.

  • Archived as presented · sealed
  • Holds together for decades
  • Retention begins at finishing
  • Retrievable, not reassembled

A question of scaleHow many records leave your office each month with a signature or a seal on them, and who finishes them today?

The configurations

Every configuration produces the same sealed record. The assessment matches the configuration to your record volume, thickness, copies, users and locations.

Implementation

Included with every system.

The recommendation is only the beginning. Every system includes the work needed to establish a written house standard and train the people who will use it.

  1. Workflow assessment

    One record followed from printer to recipient, documented.

  2. Right sized recommendation

    The configuration matched to volume, thickness, copies and users.

  3. On site installation

    Installed, configured and proven where the records are produced.

  4. Team training and certification

    Chain of custody training for the people who prepare the records.

  5. One page operating guide

    The whole procedure, readable at the machine.

  6. A written house standard

    The finished record defined once, for every office and every user.

  7. First record supervision

    The first live record completed together, to the standard.

  8. Follow up quality check

    A scheduled return visit against the written standard.

Support
